proposals.title: Amendment to Leadership Structure
proposals.author: 0x6a2404b576ADA1A1E41A2145EebE5d8DFD3cD7cb
proposals.body:
Governance Structure & Merit-Based Operational Leadership
Constitutional Amendment 

Proposal
Replacement of Existing Leadership Positions

Upon adoption of this amendment, the existing generic Leadership positions established by the Constitution shall be replaced by the following Operational Leadership portfolios:

1. Treasurer
Treasury administration
Budget monitoring
Multisignature coordination
Treasury reporting
Approved treasury asset management oversight

2. Governance & Proposals Officer
Proposal administration
Governance documentation
Proposal compliance
Governance policy administration
Governance reporting

3. Technical & Ecosystem Liaison
Technical coordination
Foundation/Core Team liaison
Infrastructure oversight
Developer coordination
Ecosystem partnerships

4. Community & Communications Officer
Community engagement
Governance announcements
Documentation
Education
Contributor coordination
Community communications

5. Strategy & Performance Officer
Strategic planning
KPI monitoring
Initiative tracking
Quarterly performance reporting
Continuous governance improvement

These positions replace the existing generic Leadership positions and provide clearly defined operational responsibilities.

The replacement of position titles is intended to improve organisational clarity and accountability only and does not alter the governance authority of the High Council or the constitutional powers of the DAO community.

The names and responsibilities of Operational Leadership portfolios may only be amended by an approved constitutional amendment unless the Constitution expressly provides otherwise.

Executive Summary
This proposal clarifies the governance structure of the Redbelly Community DAO by distinguishing between elected governance positions and appointed operational leadership positions.

The High Council will continue to be elected by the community and retain governance authority.
Operational Leadership positions will instead be appointed through a transparent, merit-based process, recognising that these positions primarily perform operational and administrative functions requiring appropriate skills, experience and availability.

This proposal preserves democratic governance while strengthening the operational capability, accountability and continuity of the DAO.

Background
The Constitution currently provides for elected High Council and Leadership positions.

Experience has demonstrated that Leadership positions perform operational rather than governance functions. These roles often require specialised skills and ongoing commitment that may not always be reflected through popularity-based elections.

This proposal aligns the governance framework with the original intent of the Constitution by ensuring governance remains democratic while operational responsibilities are undertaken by suitably qualified contributors.

Problem & Rationale
Operational Leadership positions are responsible for functions such as:
Treasury administration
Governance administration
Proposal management
Technical coordination
Ecosystem liaison
Community engagement
Strategic planning
These responsibilities are better suited to transparent merit-based appointments than popularity-based elections.
The community should continue electing those responsible for governance while enabling operational roles to be filled according to competence and capability.

Objectives
This proposal seeks to:
Preserve democratic governance.
Improve operational capability.
Strengthen accountability.
Improve governance continuity.
Ensure operational positions are filled by suitably qualified contributors.
Increase transparency of appointments.
Reduce operational risk.
Improve long-term sustainability.

Proposed Constitutional Amendment
Governance Structure
High Council

The High Council shall continue to be elected by the DAO community.

The High Council remains responsible for:
Governance oversight
Constitutional compliance
Treasury oversight
Strategic governance
Appointment oversight
Accountability to the community

This proposal does not alter the number of High Council positions established elsewhere in the Constitution.

Operational Leadership
The following positions shall become appointed Operational Leadership positions:
Treasurer
Governance & Proposals Officer
Technical & Ecosystem Liaison
Community & Communications Officer
Strategy & Performance Officer

These positions perform administrative and operational functions and do not independently exercise governance authority unless expressly authorised by the Constitution or an approved DAO proposal.
 
Appointments should seek to match each Operational Leadership portfolio with individuals possessing relevant qualifications, experience or demonstrated capability appropriate to the responsibilities of that portfolio.
_______________________________________________________________________________
Appointment Process
Operational Leadership appointments shall be made by the High Council through majority resolution following an open merit-based recruitment process. Appointment decisions, including the reasons for selection, shall be published to the community. Any community member may challenge an appointment through the Governance Appeals & Review Policy where they believe the appointment process has not been conducted in accordance with the Constitution or approved Governance Policies.
Where an elected position remains vacant, or where insufficient suitably qualified candidates are available, the High Council may appoint a suitably qualified individual to serve until the next scheduled election, subject to transparency requirements.

Appointments should consider:
Relevant experience
Demonstrated capability
Governance participation
Availability
Integrity
Communication skills
Absence of material conflicts of interest

Recruitment Process
Appointments should normally include:
Public expression of interest
Published selection criteria
Opportunity for self-nomination
Transparent appointment decision
Publication of appointment reasons

Terms of Appointment
Operational Leadership appointments should normally:
Be for a six (6) month term with one extension.
Remain eligible for reappointment.
Be reviewed annually.
Remain accountable to the High Council.

Responsibilities
Operational Leadership shall:
Fulfil the responsibilities of their assigned portfolio.
Publish periodic activity reports.
Maintain governance documentation.
Support community transparency.
Cooperate with other leadership portfolios.
Act in accordance with the Constitution, Governance Policies and Code of Conduct.
Inactivity
An Operational Leadership member may be considered inactive where they have failed to meaningfully participate in the responsibilities of their appointed role for a continuous period of thirty (30) days without reasonable explanation or prior notification to the High Council.
Meaningful participation may include:
Responding to governance matters.
Undertaking the responsibilities of the position.
Attending scheduled leadership meetings where reasonably practicable.
Providing required reports or updates.
The High Council may extend this period where reasonable circumstances exist, including illness, family responsibilities, employment commitments or other exceptional circumstances.
Where a member is determined inactive under this clause, the High Council may declare the position vacant by majority resolution.

Performance Review
An Operational Leadership appointment may be terminated for unsatisfactory performance or serious misconduct, including material breach of the Code of Conduct, where the High Council has determined, by majority resolution, that the member has persistently failed to fulfil the responsibilities of their appointed role despite having been provided with reasonable opportunity to address identified concerns.

Removal Process
Prior to removal, the Operational Leadership member should:
Be informed of the concerns.
Be provided an opportunity to respond.
Be given reasonable opportunity to address the concerns where appropriate.
Following consideration of all relevant information, the High Council may remove the appointment by majority resolution.
The decision and reasons for removal should be documented and made available to the community, except where confidentiality is required by law or to protect personal privacy.

Appeals
Any Operational Leadership member removed under this provision may request a review under the Governance Appeals & Review Policy.

Vacancies
Temporary Appointment of Foundation Personnel
Where:
no suitably qualified community applicant is available following a documented recruitment process; or
an Operational Leadership position remains vacant following reasonable efforts to appoint a community member; and
the continued vacancy presents a material operational risk to the DAO,
the High Council may request that the Redbelly Foundation nominate a suitably qualified employee or contractor to temporarily perform the responsibilities of the vacant Operational Leadership position.
Any such appointment shall:
be temporary only;
ineligible for filling the Treasurer role specifically due to conflict of interest
be approved by the High Council by majority resolution;
not exceed twelve (12) months without further DAO approval;
remain subject to the Constitution, Governance Policies and Code of Conduct;
be publicly announced together with the reasons for the appointment.
Where an Operational Leadership position becomes vacant, the High Council may appoint an interim replacement by majority resolution until the position is filled through the normal appointment process.
This proposal does not alter constitutional provisions relating to elected High Council vacancies.
Governance Principles
Operational Leadership exists to support the effective administration of the DAO.
Appointments should be based primarily upon competence, experience, integrity and the ability to fulfil the responsibilities of the role rather than popularity.
Community governance shall continue to be exercised through:
Snapshot voting
Constitutional amendments
Governance proposals
Election of the High Council
Benefits
This proposal:
Preserves democratic governance.
Improves operational capability.
Strengthens accountability.
Reduces operational risk.
Improves governance continuity.
Aligns appointments with required expertise.
Increases transparency.
Supports long-term sustainability.
Risk & Mitigation
Risk
Mitigation
Perception of reduced decentralisation
High Council remains fully elected by the community.
Perception of favouritism
Transparent recruitment process and published appointment reasons.
Poor appointments
Annual reviews, majority High Council oversight and defined removal process.
Reduced community involvement
Community retains governance authority through Snapshot voting and High Council elections.
Constitutional Compatibility
This proposal clarifies the distinction between governance oversight and operational administration.
It preserves community governance while strengthening the operational capability of the DAO.
Budget
0 USDT / 0 RBNT
Decision Requested
Approve the amendment to distinguish elected governance positions from appointed Operational Leadership positions, adopt the transparent merit-based appointment framework described in this proposal, and authorise consequential amendments to related governance documents and role descriptions.

proposals.title: DAO Proposal: Increase Governance Accessibility and Protect Contributor Privacy
proposals.author: 0xA4811219b12CE85B377Cd8197b929e98d1C3CdE1
proposals.body:
**DAO Proposal: Increase Governance Accessibility and Protect Contributor Privacy  
Proposal Title  
Remove Voting Whitelist Requirement and Remove Geographic Restrictions for General DAO Members**

Submitted By  
@rainbowmagician1  
0xA4811219b12CE85B377Cd8197b929e98d1C3CdE1

  
**Summary**
This proposal seeks to improve accessibility and participation within the Redbelly Community DAO by:  
Removing the whitelist requirement for participation in DAO voting.  
Removing geographic restrictions for General DAO Members.  
Maintaining all existing geographic limitations for High Council Members and General DAO Leadership.  
The proposal aims to lower barriers to participation, better protect contributor privacy, and further support the DAO's long-term goal of progressive decentralisation.

**Problem & Rationale**
The Redbelly Community DAO Constitution states that the DAO exists to steward growth, adoption, and decentralisation of the community while progressively decentralising governance as the contributor base matures. It also identifies Progressive Decentralisation and Fair Access, with Structured Onboarding as founding principles.  
The current governance framework also establishes geographic limitations for leadership positions to ensure decentralisation and geographic diversity.  
This proposal does not seek to modify those leadership protections.  
Instead, it proposes that these geographic limitations should apply only to High Council Members and General DAO Leadership, allowing General DAO Members to participate regardless of country of residence.  
Additionally, removing the voting whitelist would reduce onboarding friction and better respect contributor privacy by avoiding unnecessary disclosure of personal information for members who simply wish to participate in governance.  
This proposal is intended to:  
Lower barriers to governance participation.  
Encourage wider community engagement.  
Improve contributor privacy.  
Preserve decentralisation safeguards where they matter most—leadership positions.  
Note: The uploaded governance documents do not explicitly document a voting whitelist requirement. If the whitelist exists as an operational or Snapshot configuration rather than a constitutional rule, that implementation should be referenced during governance discussion.

**Objectives & Strategic Fit**
This proposal supports the DAO by:  
Increasing governance participation.  
Reducing onboarding friction.  
Improving contributor privacy.  
Encouraging greater international participation.  
Supporting progressive decentralisation.  
Maintaining existing geographic protections for High Council and General DAO Leadership.

**Scope of Work & Deliverables**
Milestone 1  
Remove the whitelist requirement for participation in DAO voting (where technically applicable).  
Milestone 2  
Amend governance documentation so that geographic restrictions apply only to:  
High Council Members  
General DAO Leadership  
General DAO Members would no longer be subject to regional eligibility restrictions.  
Milestone 3  
Publish updated governance documentation and communicate the changes through official DAO channels.

**Budget & Payment Structure**
USDT Requested: 0  
RBNT Requested: 0  
No treasury funding is requested.

**ROI & Impact**
Success will be measured by:  
Increased number of DAO participants.  
Higher Snapshot voter participation.  
Greater geographic diversity among contributors.  
Reduced onboarding friction for new members.  
Improved contributor privacy by removing unnecessary whitelist requirements.

**Oversight & Accountability**  
Implementation will be overseen by the High Council.  
Any documentation updates should be published publicly following the existing governance process: publication of revised constitution, publication of updated handbook, confirmation when snapshot settings (if any) have been updated.

**Risk & Mitigation**  
Risk  
Mitigation  
Increased number of voting participants  
Existing proposal review and voting processes remain unchanged.  
Confusion regarding leadership eligibility  
Documentation will clearly state that geographic restrictions remain in place for High Council Members and General DAO Leadership.  
Governance documentation inconsistencies  
Update all affected governance documents simultaneously.

Co-Funding & Leverage  
Not applicable.

**Team & Contributors**  
Community governance proposal.

Community Involvement  
Community discussion on Discord before Snapshot submission.  
Feedback incorporated prior to voting.

Compliance & Ethical Standards  
This proposal:  
Does not request treasury funding.  
Does not modify treasury management.  
Does not change compensation models.  
Does not alter conflict-of-interest provisions.  
Preserves existing decentralisation safeguards for leadership positions.  
Supports broader community participation while respecting the DAO's governance principles.

Supporting Documents  
Redbelly Community DAO Constitution v1.3  
Community DAO Handbook

Decision Requested  
Approve the following governance changes:  
Remove the whitelist requirement for participation in DAO voting (if applicable within DAO operations).  
Remove geographic restrictions for General DAO Members.  
Retain all existing geographic limitations for High Council Members and General DAO Leadership.  
Update the Constitution and related governance documentation to reflect these changes.  
Publish the revised governance documentation following the existing amendment process.

![open.png](ipfs://bafkreihqbu7kqdsmhiyx2smamqc6ar7rjqu24clvabrhdfdfqkwdndpvcm)

**Name:** *(Berlin)*

**Summary **

This proposal requests funding of **$350 USDT per month** for the continued development, hosting, maintenance, and operation of the official Redbelly DAO Discord Bot, along with ongoing Discord community management and engagement activities.

The bot is designed to become a central hub for DAO members by simplifying governance, improving communication, and supporting contributor coordination. It also provides a foundation for future DAO features such as task management, contributor notifications, and community engagement.


** Problem & Rationale**

As the Redbelly DAO grows, community members use several different platforms to access governance updates, participate in discussions, and coordinate work. This can make it difficult to stay informed and engaged.

A dedicated Discord bot provides a single place where members can access governance information, receive important notifications, and, in the future, manage contributor tasks without leaving Discord.

Combining bot development with community management ensures that both the technical platform and the community continue to grow together.



**Objectives**

The objectives of this proposal are to:

* Improve communication within the DAO.
* Increase participation in governance.
* Provide automated notifications for DAO activities.
* Build a task management system for contributors.
* Support onboarding and engagement of community members.
* Create a more active and organized Discord community.



** Current Features**

The bot already includes:

* Interactive DAO dashboard
* Live Snapshot proposal integration
* Active and past proposal browsing
* Proposal details and voting information
* Wallet linking
* Member profiles
* Participation leaderboard
* Automatic notifications for new proposals
* Voting reminder notifications



** Planned Features**

During this funding period, development will focus on expanding the bot with:

**Task Management**

* Members can view available DAO tasks.
* Members can accept tasks.
* Members can submit completed work.
* Administrators can approve or reject submitted tasks.
* Automatic notifications when new tasks become available.
* Status updates for accepted and completed tasks.

** Community Management**

* Discord moderation and support.
* New member onboarding.
* Community announcements.
* Community games and engagement events.
* General server management.
* Regular improvements based on community feedback.



 **Deliverables**

Each month includes:

* 24/7 bot hosting.
* Ongoing maintenance and bug fixes.
* New feature development.
* Discord community management.
* Community engagement activities.
* Technical support.
* Performance monitoring.
* Regular updates and improvements.



** Budget**

| Service                      | Monthly Cost |
| ---------------------------- | -----------: |
| Bot Hosting & Infrastructure |    $100 USDT |
| Development & Maintenance    |    $100 USDT |
| Discord Community Management |    $100 USDT |
| Community Games & Events     |     $50 USDT |

**Total Requested**

**$350 USDT per month**

Payments are requested monthly based on continued delivery of services.



 **Success Metrics**

Success will be measured through:

* Increased community participation.
* Number of active bot users.
* Number of wallet-linked members.
* Task participation once implemented.
* Community event participation.
* Reliable bot uptime and support.
* Positive feedback from DAO members.



**Oversight & Accountability**

Monthly updates will be provided to the DAO including:

* Features delivered.
* Bot uptime.
* Community management activities.
* Planned improvements for the following month.



** Risk & Mitigation**

Potential risks include Discord API changes, hosting issues, or feature requests beyond the current scope. These will be addressed through ongoing maintenance, monitoring, backups, and regular updates.



** Community Involvement**

Community feedback will guide future improvements. Members will be encouraged to suggest new features, report issues, and participate in testing to ensure the bot continues to meet the DAO's needs.



** Decision Requested**

Approve funding of **$350 USDT per month** for the development, hosting, maintenance, and ongoing management of the Redbelly DAO Discord Bot and Discord community services.

This proposal aims to provide the DAO with a reliable platform for governance, communication, contributor coordination, and community engagement, while laying the groundwork for future features such as integrated task management and automated contributor workflows.

proposals.title: Temporary Suspension of new treasury-funded activities of the Redbelly Community DAO Until Ecosystem Readiness
proposals.author: 0xA4811219b12CE85B377Cd8197b929e98d1C3CdE1
proposals.body:
Submitted by
@Rainbowmagician1
0xA4811219b12CE85B377Cd8197b929e98d1C3CdE1


# Summary
This proposal seeks to temporarily suspend the operational activities of the Redbelly Community DAO until the broader Redbelly ecosystem reaches a level of maturity where the DAO can efficiently achieve its stated objectives.
The proposal is intended to preserve treasury resources, reduce operational overhead, and allow the DAO to resume when there is a stronger foundation for meaningful community-led initiatives.
No existing approved obligations would be affected.


# Problem & Rationale
The Constitution states that the Community DAO exists to support the growth, adoption and decentralisation of the Redbelly Community DAO.
The proposer believes that the ecosystem is still in an early stage where maintaining continuous treasury-funded activity may not currently provide the highest return for the community.
A temporary suspension would allow the DAO to preserve financial resources and avoid unnecessary expenditure until conditions better support effective community governance and measurable outcomes.
This proposal is intended as a treasury preservation measure rather than a permanent closure.


# Objectives
Preserve DAO treasury assets.
Reduce unnecessary operational expenditure.
Complete all currently approved commitments.
Pause funding of new initiatives during the suspension.
Resume DAO operations through a future governance vote when ecosystem readiness improves.
Working Group:
 Governance / Treasury

# Scope of Work
If approved:
Phase 1 (Immediately)
Complete all approved proposals already under execution.
Complete any outstanding contributor payments already approved.
All proposals approved by Snapshot before the suspension takes effect will continue through completion under their approved terms.
Phase 2
Suspend:
New treasury-funded proposals.
New grant programs.
New bounty programs.
New discretionary treasury spending.
Continue:
Treasury security.
Treasury transparency.
Governance record keeping.

# Timeline
Immediately following approval:
Week 1–2
Finalize outstanding obligations.
Week 3
Publish treasury status.
Suspension Period
Treasury remains secured.
No new funded initiatives.
Review
Every six months, the High Council publishes a readiness assessment and recommendation. The decision to continue the suspension or reopen DAO operations is then put to a community vote.

# Budget
No new budget requested.
Expected outcome:
Reduction of future operational expenditure.
Preservation of remaining treasury assets.

# Strategic Fit
This proposal aligns with:
Responsible treasury management.
Long-term sustainability.
Governance efficiency.
Transparency.
These objectives are consistent with the Constitution's emphasis on responsible treasury management and long-term sustainability.

# Oversight & Accountability
Oversight by:
High Council
Treasury multisig
Reporting:
Treasury dashboard remains public.
Six-month readiness review.
Public governance updates continue.

KPIs
Success will be measured by:
100% completion of existing approved obligations.
No unapproved treasury expenditure during suspension.
Treasury transparency maintained.
Preservation of treasury assets.
Governance review completed every six months.

Risks
Risk
Reduced community activity.
Mitigation
Community discussion channels remain open.

Risk
Loss of contributor engagement.
Mitigation
DAO may be reactivated through governance at any time after the first 6 month period.

Risk
Delayed ecosystem initiatives.
Mitigation
Only treasury-funded initiatives are paused.

Community Involvement
This proposal should be discussed publicly on Discord before Snapshot, in accordance with the DAO governance process.
Community feedback during the discussion period may be incorporated before the final vote.

Compliance
The proposal does not request payments to contributors or external organizations.
It does not modify treasury ownership.
It does not affect previously approved commitments.
Any constitutional changes required for implementation should follow the amendment process described in the Constitution.

# Decision Requested
Approve the temporary suspension of new treasury-funded activities of the Redbelly Community DAO until a future governance vote determines that the ecosystem has reached sufficient maturity to resume normal DAO operations.

**Submitted by:** njay (@njaybby)
**Working Group:** Community (Primary) · Marketing · Research · Builders
**Full Proposal:** [Read the full document here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19kdy73N5xi8uWlX5JgflfqJNiGSdMv3b/view?usp=drivesdk)

---

## What is this?

The Redbelly DAO has skilled, motivated community members with nowhere structured to direct their energy. This proposal creates a **Community Task Board**, a system where contributors can pick up real tasks, do real work, and earn RBNT rewards for it. Documentation, research, content, developer tools, ecosystem building, and more.

The task board runs on the existing DAO website infrastructure. No new platforms. No bloat. Just a structured way to get things done.

---

## Why now?

- The DAO treasury has resources but no clear pathway for community contributors beyond large one-off proposals
- Developers building DAO infrastructure have no formal audit or peer review loop
- Documentation and tutorials for builders are lacking, slowing ecosystem growth
- Project Acacia Q1 2026 report drops soon, a time-sensitive research opportunity we should not miss
- Other L1s are building comprehensive developer ecosystems. We should too.

---

## How it works

**6 task categories:**

- **A. Documentation & Tutorials:** guides, video tutorials, developer onboarding content
- **B. Content & Community:** infographics, case studies, Twitter threads, Scout role for ecosystem content
- **C. Research & Analysis:** competitive intelligence, RWA market research, Project Acacia deep-dive
- **D. Developer Work:** smart contract templates, CI/CD tooling, peer review and audit of DAO-built infrastructure
- **E. Ecosystem Building:** compliance templates, partnership research, service provider directories
- **F. Strategic Coordination:** monthly education and technical working meetings

**Anyone can propose tasks.** A Google Form will be set up in Week 1 for open nominations from community members and core team alike.

**All payments in RBNT,** except video production tasks which include a 30% USDT component to cover software costs.

---

## Budget

Two separate budgets. No conversion between them.

| Budget | Quarterly Cap | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RBNT | $4,500 USD equivalent | All tasks except video. Fixed in RBNT at proposal approval using 7-day moving average, reset each quarter. |
| USDT | $500 | Video task production costs only (30% component) |
| **Total** | **$5,000** | Hard quarterly cap. Auto-pause if either budget is exhausted. |

---

## Rollout

**Phase 1 (Months 1-3):** Pilot with 10-12 tasks, 3-5 reviewers, quality standards established.
**Phase 2 (Months 4-6):** Scale to 20-25 tasks/month, bug bounty program launches, reputation tiers introduced.
**Phase 3 (Months 7-12):** Stable operations, contributor pipeline feeding reviewer roles, outputs integrated into official docs.

Quarterly DAO votes determine continuation at each phase.

---

## Accountability

- Every deliverable reviewed before payment
- Weekly updates in a dedicated Discord channel
- Monthly report across Discord, X, and Telegram
- Quarterly review with DAO vote
- Hard kill switch conditions if quality drops or budget is hit

---

## Contributors

This proposal was developed collaboratively. Compiled and structured by njay, built on ideas and contributions from **Godwin, Debanked, Benny, Buffy, and Rainbow.**

---

## Full Document

Want the complete picture? Budget breakdowns, task pricing, KPIs, risk mitigation, reviewer structure, and more:

[Read the full proposal](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19kdy73N5xi8uWlX5JgflfqJNiGSdMv3b/view?usp=drivesdk)

---

*By voting FOR, the DAO commits to building lasting infrastructure, systematic security auditing, strategic intelligence, and clear contribution pathways, all while aligning contributor incentives with network success through RBNT-denominated rewards.*

DAO PROPOSAL  
Redbelly Official Mascot Design Competition  by @debanked 
Open to the full Redbelly community and ecosystem

1.  Proposal Summary  
    This proposal launches a DAO-wide open competition to design an official Redbelly DAO mascot, with prizes awarded to winning entries and the DAO acquiring full usage rights to the selected character. The goal is to produce a high-quality, community-created, reusable brand asset suitable for marketing campaigns, educational content, live events, and ongoing social media presence.
    
2.  Problem & Rationale  
    Redbelly currently lacks a distinct and recognizable visual mascot that can humanize the brand, improve recall, and be reused consistently across all channels. Without such an asset, marketing materials rely on abstract or generic visuals that fail to build emotional connection with the audience.
    

A community competition directly addresses this gap while generating additional value:  
Encourages broad participation from designers and creators across the ecosystem  
Surfaces diverse creative ideas that internal teams may not produce alone  
Strengthens DAO culture by giving members a tangible stake in brand identity  
Ensures legitimacy through transparent community selection rather than top-down appointment

3.  Objectives & Strategic Fit  
    Objectives  
    Create an official DAO-owned mascot with full perpetual usage rights  
    Engage the community in a meaningful creative process  
    Generate reusable design assets for long-term brand use  
    Strengthen Redbelly's brand identity and visual consistency across channels  
    Strategic Fit  
    Community WG — drives engagement, incentivizes participation, and rewards contributors  
    Marketing WG — delivers a brand storytelling asset for campaigns and social media  
    DAO-wide goals — supports adoption and awareness through memorable visual identity
    
4.  Scope of Work & Deliverables
   ![IMG_7256.jpg](ipfs://bafkreihz7rf5bisepqdejxyw7nz3xgjab2mz27n33j7acckvwlsmxa7eoe) 

Final deliverables include: mascot asset pack (highest quality PNG, SVG, vector formats), official style guide, finalist archive, and a final summary report. Design platform files should also be handed over i.e Procreate, Photoshop etcétera

5.  Budget Alignment & Limits
    
![IMG_7257.jpg](ipfs://bafkreicgchpl3kwatm7fqss6ydtxrskkr2vs72naggi2kjy7nq4fnbp7me)
Budget notes:  
is reserved strictly for external prize payments and participants finalization — no personal expenses or unverifiable activities  
RBNT is used exclusively for incentives — no token purchases  
Total request remains well below 25% of the Working Group's annual allocation  
Full cost justification is embedded in the payout structure above  
DAO reserve policy is respected — no draw on emergency reserves

6.  Payment & Payout Structure  
    All payments are milestone-based — no upfront disbursements  
    RBNT finalist incentives released only after shortlist is verified and published (Phase 3)  
    USDT prizes released only after final asset delivery and IP rights transfer are confirmed (Phase 4)  
    RBNT community pool distributed post-competition based on verified participation  
    Full payout tables published publicly before the competition launches  
    Supervisor validates each milestone before any payout is approved
    
7.  Oversight & Accountability  
    An independent lead reviewer (Buffy) will be nominated from the DAO or Marketing Working Group prior to launch. This individual will not be eligible for any prizes and carries no financial interest in the outcome. The proposer will also be ineligible.
    

Oversight responsibilities include:  
Enforcing competition rules and eligibility criteria  
Verifying originality and intellectual property declarations for all submissions  
Approving the shortlist before public voting opens  
Validating final asset delivery and rights transfer before USDT disbursement  
Approving all milestone payouts before funds are released  
Publishing weekly progress updates in DAO channels  
Submitting a final public report upon competition close

8.  Impact & Measurement (KPIs)

    Final report published within one week of competition close
    
9.  Risk & Mitigation
    ![IMG_7258.jpg](ipfs://bafkreifwbki3oldf4rv5ouggzkhhswouyfojr7i47vhxv7mu7hhl6k7ifa)

10.  Co-Funding & Leverage  
    Community creators contribute their design work in exchange for prizes, meaning the DAO receives significant creative value at a fraction of market rate for commissioned artwork. The winning mascot becomes a long-term, reusable asset deployable across social media, events, documentation, education materials, and future brand campaigns — all at no additional cost.
    

Any future extensions such as animated versions, merchandise, or NFT variants would require separate DAO proposals and would not be covered by this budget.

11.  Contribution Equity  
    Prizes are distributed across multiple winners — no single individual receives a dominant share  
    RBNT rewards are spread across all verified finalists and community participants  
    The proposer and all oversight members are explicitly ineligible to win any prizes or finalist incentives  
    No single contributor holds multiple lead roles under this proposal without separate DAO approval
    
12.  Compliance & Ethical Standards  
    No financial advice is offered or implied by this proposal or competition process  
    The competition process is fully transparent — rules, scoring, and results published publicly  
    Only original, first-party work is accepted; all submissions must include an originality declaration  
    The DAO receives full, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free usage rights to the winning mascot upon prize payment  
    All finalist and final assets stored in DAO-accessible repositories for community use  
    Consistent with DAO code of conduct; no regulatory or reputational risks identified
    
13.  Community Involvement  
    Open submissions from all community members and ecosystem participants.  
    Community voting on the final shortlist — one verifiable wallet, one vote  
    Public discussion threads maintained throughout the competition period  
    All final assets shared openly for DAO-wide community use post-competition  
    This proposal itself is open for community feedback and co-authorship prior to formal submission
    

14.  Decision Requested
    

Approve 467,570 RBNT to run the DAO-governed Redbelly Community Mascot Design Competition — with milestone-based payouts, independent oversight, transparent community voting, and full perpetual IP rights acquisition for DAO-wide use.

developers,
validators,
community
institutions, and
potential partners

Create evergreen YouTube videos that simplify complex topics for non-technical

proposals.title: Community Consultation Policy — Authorization of Proposal Discussions in Non-Official Groups
proposals.author: 0xA4811219b12CE85B377Cd8197b929e98d1C3CdE1
proposals.body:
Relevant Working Group
Community, research, development, marketing, partnership

Proposal Summary 
This proposal seeks DAO approval to officially authorize the discussion of any DAO proposal in non-official groups — before, during, and after submission — while maintaining that only DAO members can vote through official governance channels.

Problem & Rationale
Proposal discussions already occur naturally across multiple Telegram groups or X or any socials platforms, but without an explicit rule, leading to confusion and unnecessary moderation friction.
Many community members wish to contribute ideas without taking on formal DAO roles.
Clarifying that these discussions are allowed increases transparency, supports decentralisation, and improves proposal quality without affecting official governance procedures.
This policy protects the integrity of the vote while expanding constructive community participation.

Objectives & Strategic Fit
Confirm that all discussions related to DAO proposals are allowed outside official channels.
Reinforce that only official governance channels handle voting and binding decisions.
Encourage broader participation and community input, fully aligned with the Community Working Group’s mission.
Strengthen decentralisation and transparency, in line with Redbelly DAO’s Founding Principles.

Scope of Work & Deliverables
(No operational work or budget — simple governance clarification.)

**Framework (for confirmation by the DAO)
If approved, the DAO formally adopts the following principles:**

1. Free and open discussion
Any DAO proposal may be discussed freely in any non-official community group, before, during, or after submission.
2. Voting restricted to official DAO channels
Binding votes and decisions occur only in Snapshot and official governance systems.
3. Freedom of debate
Community groups may host questions, criticisms, commentary, summaries, or general discussion on any proposal.
4. Participation of DAO roles
Council members, Leaders, and Contributors may join these discussions for clarification purposes, without directing voting outcomes.
5. Proposal refinement allowed
Authors may freely use feedback from non-official groups to improve or rewrite their proposals before or after submission.
6. No penalties for external discussion
No member may face moderation action or consequences solely for discussing a proposal in a non-official group.
7. Recognition of community diversity
The DAO acknowledges and values the multiplicity of external groups, cultures, and perspectives across the Redbelly ecosystem.
8. Optional clarification disclaimer
Groups may use this line for transparency: “This is an open discussion. Voting happens only on Snapshot.”

Team & Contributors
No operational team or contributors required.

proposals.title: Community Code of Conduct
proposals.author: 0x130ce6E5f3D129B1Ce34102AFAC671619EB009E3
proposals.body:
# **Context**
The Redbelly DAO has grown rapidly, with contributors engaging across Discord, Telegram, forums, Snapshot, and in-person events. While this growth is positive, it also increases the importance of maintaining shared standards of behavior, respect, and accountability.

At present, the DAO does not have a formal Community Code of Conduct. This creates risk of misaligned expectations, unresolved disputes, and reputational harm if inappropriate behavior occurs. Other leading DAOs (ENS, Gitcoin, Optimism) have adopted codes of conduct to set clear norms and provide a framework for enforcement.

To strengthen community trust, protect contributors, and support healthy governance, we propose adopting a formal Redbelly DAO Community Code of Conduct.

# **Proposed Community Code of Conduct**
Core Principles
- Respect – Debate ideas, not people.
- Transparency – Share openly unless bound by confidentiality.
- Accountability – Take responsibility for your words, actions, and proposals.
- Inclusivity – Value diverse perspectives; no harassment or discrimination.
- Constructiveness – Critiques should be solution-oriented.
- Integrity – Avoid conflicts of interest and misuse of DAO resources.

Expected Behaviors
- Professional and respectful engagement, even in disagreement.
- Use of evidence and reasoning when critiquing or proposing.
- Welcoming newcomers with guidance and support.
- Following proposal and governance processes in good faith.
- Protecting community security (no scams, phishing, impersonation).

Unacceptable Behaviors
- Harassment, hate speech, personal attacks.
- Spamming or shilling unrelated projects.
- Manipulation of governance processes (Sybil attacks, undisclosed vote buying).
- Misrepresentation of DAO affiliation or confidential info.

Enforcement
- Warnings – for minor breaches.
- Temporary Restrictions – for repeated or significant violations.
- Permanent Removal – for severe misconduct (fraud, harassment, governance manipulation).
- Appeals – via DAO-designated review pod or council.

# **Decision Requested**
DAO members are asked to vote on whether to adopt the Redbelly DAO Community Code of Conduct as outlined above.

✅ Yes – Adopt the Community Code of Conduct
❌ No – Do not adopt the Community Code of Conduct

proposals.title: Adoption of Standardised Proposal Evaluation Criteria
proposals.author: 0x130ce6E5f3D129B1Ce34102AFAC671619EB009E3
proposals.body:
# **Context**
As the DAO scales, it is important that all new proposals are reviewed consistently and fairly. To achieve this, we propose adopting a standardised set of evaluation criteria that pod leaders will use when assessing incoming proposals. This ensures transparency, reduces subjectivity, and gives proposers clear expectations of what is required.

# **What’s Being Proposed**
Pod leaders agree to adopt the following Proposal Review Checklist as the baseline framework when evaluating new submissions. Leaders should flag concerns where criteria are not met and provide constructive feedback to proposers.

# **DAO Proposal Review Checklist**
*1. Budget Alignment & Limits*
- Clear separation of USDT (external spend) and RBNT (internal rewards).
- Request does not exceed 25% of the working group’s annual allocation.
- Budget proportional to workload/deliverables.
- Cost breakdown or justification included.
⚠️ Flag if missing USDT/RBNT split, excessive allocation, or weak justification.

*2. Payment & Payout Structure*
- Payouts milestone-based or post-completion.
- Upfront requests require clear justification.
- Milestones tied to deliverables.
⚠️ Flag if large upfront payments lack justification or no milestone structure provided.

*3. Strategic Fit*
- Alignment with one of the three working groups (Community, Marketing, Developers/Builders).
- Clear link to DAO-wide goals (adoption, awareness, infrastructure growth).
⚠️ Flag if alignment unclear or goals vague.

*4. Feasibility & Timeline*
- Timeline with milestones/deliverables provided.
- Scope achievable with proposed budget/resources.
- No duplication of existing efforts.
⚠️ Flag if timeline absent, milestones vague, or scope unrealistic.

*5. Oversight & Accountability*
- Independent reviewer/oversight lead nominated.
- Monthly updates planned in DAO channels.
⚠️ Flag if oversight or communication plan missing.

*6. Impact & Measurement*
- KPIs or measurable success criteria included.
- Midpoint and final review methods defined.
- Long-term/community value identified.
⚠️ Flag if no success criteria or only short-term focus.

*7. Risk & Mitigation*
- Key risks identified.
- Mitigation strategies outlined.
⚠️ Flag if no risks or mitigation described.

*8. Co-Funding & Leverage*
- Matching funds, sponsorships, or in-kind contributions noted.
⚠️ Flag if no leverage (not a dealbreaker, but relevant).

*9. Contribution Equity*
- No single contributor dominating payouts.
- Proposer not holding multiple paid lead roles without justification.
⚠️ Flag if payouts concentrated with same individual(s).

*10. Compliance & Ethical Standards*
- No regulatory/reputational risks.
- Consistency with DAO’s code of conduct.
⚠️ Flag if unclear or non-compliant activities proposed.

*11. Community Involvement*
- Evidence of discussion with community members.
- Presence of co-authors or collaborators.
⚠️ Flag if no signs of community input.


# **Decision Requested**
Pod leaders are asked to ratify this checklist as the official evaluation framework for proposal reviews.

✅ Yes – adopt this checklist as the standard review criteria.
❌ No – do not adopt.

If adopted, all future proposals will be reviewed against these criteria to ensure consistency and accountability across the DAO.
